positions.label: B2B 节气 operations pack to small food businesses, sold by 1:1 outreach

reasoning.revenue_potential: ¥199/quarter x 20 buyers is ~¥14k/yr against ¥39 x 100 = ¥3.9k, and the buyer has a budget line rather than discretionary spend. The buyer loses money weekly by getting seasonality wrong, which is the only profile in this whole set with non-trivial willingness to pay.
reasoning.evidence: Structurally strong reasoning, but zero direct evidence that these buyers exist for THIS product - no agent researched B2B demand and the Red Team cited none. Tier 7 opinion resting on Tier 6 category logic. Capped at 5; it is the highest-variance position here.
reasoning.cost: Three hours and ¥0 for the full test. The content asset is nearly identical to what all nine consumer plans already require building, so it reuses rather than adds work.
reasoning.speed_to_learn: Ten sends, replies within days. 处暑 is ~5 days out, giving a natural deadline. Fastest true/false in the set by a wide margin.
reasoning.reversibility: Nothing is built, published, registered or spent. If all ten ignore it, the founder has lost one afternoon.
reasoning.brand_risk: 1:1 outreach to businesses is legitimate but sits close to cold outreach; sloppy execution reads as spam and burns local reputation in a small community. Requires approval H9 before sending. Deducted for that.

reasoning.revenue_potential: Western price norms give roughly 5x the mainland ceiling for identical content, and if it converts the entire library re-prices at USD 29-39/yr for zero extra production cost. Ceiling is real but bounded by a small addressable niche.

reasoning.cost: Two hours to stand up a Payhip or Ko-fi page and post it. No cash. The Red Team's modification - skip the 12 free weeks entirely - removes the expensive part of C's original plan.
reasoning.speed_to_learn: Seven days to a first stranger sale or silence. Tests willingness-to-pay, payment rail and community link tolerance in one move.
reasoning.reversibility: A pre-order page can be taken down. The only real exposure is refunding anyone who paid, which at this volume is trivial.
reasoning.brand_risk: Pre-selling an unbuilt product is honest ONLY with an explicit ship date and an unconditional refund offer. Without both it violates Constitution Article 8. Deducted because the honest version is materially less persuasive than the dishonest one, and that temptation is the risk.
